tapeLine: Tuesday 24 November: S&P 500 −0.50% to 7,201.09; Nasdaq Composite −1.48% (−356.03) to 23,733.54; Dow +0.85% to 50,018.70, closing above 50,000 (Yahoo Finance; Kotak Neo; Journal Arta, 24–25 Nov).
matters:
Tuesday split along the same lines as the last two sessions, in reverse again: the Dow closed above 50,000 while the Nasdaq gave back about a quarter of Monday’s 6.5% jump. Wraps tied the tech selling to AI valuation and infrastructure-spending worries and to reports of new US tariffs; Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell about 17% to $39.80 by Tuesday afternoon after warning that AI servers would pressure gross margin through fiscal 2027, and Dell fell 11.83% in the regular session before reporting (Benzinga; Seeking Alpha; Yahoo Finance, 24 Nov). Anthropic (ANT) closed −6.54% at $81.91, below its $83 IPO price on its fourth trading day (Yahoo Finance; Bloomberg; Axios, 24 Nov).

This morning futures are lower again ahead of an 8:30 a.m. ET block of October PCE, the Q3 GDP second estimate, jobless claims and durable goods, the last major data before the 8–9 Dec FOMC. Yahoo Finance’s live blog had Dow futures −0.7%, S&P 500 −1% and Nasdaq-100 −2% at one point, with a later snapshot nearer S&P −0.73% and Nasdaq-100 −1.20% (Yahoo Finance, 25 Nov). Reports say USTR may announce results of its Section 301 overcapacity investigations into 16 economies as early as this week; that rests on unnamed sources and is not confirmed (WSJ via SBS; Wisevoter, 25 Nov).

calendar.consensus: Headline 3.8% y/y; core 3.2% y/y (investingLive; Admiral Markets)

alsoOnTape: 10-year Treasury yield closed Tuesday at about 4.90% (Longbridge 4.9038%, about 4 bp lower; Investing.com 4.902%), 2-year about 4.67%, 30-year about 5.29% (Longbridge, 24 Nov). Dollar, oil and gold Tuesday levels not confirmed and left out. US markets are closed Thursday and close at 1:00 p.m. ET Friday.
overnight: Latest confirmed close — Tuesday 24 November: S&P 500 7,201.09 (−0.50%); Nasdaq Composite 23,733.54 (−1.48%); Dow 50,018.70 (+0.85%) (Yahoo Finance; Kotak Neo; Journal Arta, 24–25 Nov).

Dell — fiscal Q3 revenue $54.9 billion against about $49.3 billion expected; adjusted EPS $9.45 against about $6.59; fiscal 2027 revenue outlook raised to $202 billion; $25 billion added to buybacks. Shares −11.83% to $295.28 in the regular session, then up after hours, by 1.5% to 4.8% depending on the snapshot (Yahoo Finance; Benzinga; Investing.com, 24 Nov).
Other after-hours movers — Workday +1.79%, HP −3.32%, Autodesk +0.14% (Investing.com, 24 Nov). Results details for these three not confirmed and left out.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise — beat fiscal Q4 estimates (adjusted EPS $1.43 vs $1.29) but warned gross margin would soften through fiscal 2027 on AI server mix; shares −17.1% to $39.80 Tuesday afternoon per Benzinga, which called it the worst day since the 2015 debut; other outlets had 15–16% (Benzinga; Seeking Alpha; Invezz, 24 Nov).
Anthropic (ANT) — −6.54% to $81.91, below the $83 IPO price (Yahoo Finance; Bloomberg; Axios, 24 Nov).
deals: Sanofi / Insmed — $175 per share in cash, about $41.0 billion; about 46% premium to the 18 Nov close before deal reports, about 17.5% to the 23 Nov close; expected to close in 1H 2027 subject to shareholder and regulatory approval. Insmed shares rose about 14% (Sanofi 6-K; Bloomberg; CNBC; Axios, 24 Nov).
macro: Conference Board consumer confidence, November — 103.3, up 11.4 from a revised 91.9, highest since January 2025, against about 92.2 expected (WSJ poll). Present Situation 132.8; Expectations 83.6. Survey window 1–17 Nov (Conference Board via PR Newswire; Bloomberg; Advisor Perspectives, 24 Nov).

Section 301 — USTR’s overcapacity probe, opened 11 Mar, covers 16 economies including China, the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Mexico and India. Results reported as possible this week; no rates published (White & Case; WSJ via SBS; Wisevoter, 25 Nov).
Fed — previews describe October PCE as the last major inflation read before the 8–9 Dec meeting, with a December hike widely priced (investingLive; StockTitan, 24–25 Nov).
flow: Breadth, dealer gamma, put-call and skew are paid data and are not on this page.

regime.tag: Monday’s tech-led rebound partly unwound Tuesday while the Dow set a close above 50,000, into a data-heavy Wednesday before the holiday.
regime.sizing: Wednesday’s 8:30 block lands on a thin holiday tape with futures already lower; how PCE compares with the 3.8% / 3.2% consensus is the open question.

secondOrder: The Dow and Nasdaq have now moved in opposite directions or by very different amounts for three straight sessions. Server makers diverged on margins: HPE fell on a margin warning while Dell beat and raised. Consumer confidence jumped to a near two-year high on the same day Anthropic broke its IPO price. Observations, not forecasts.

scorecard.text: The prior brief carried a November consumer confidence consensus of 92.0–92.5. It printed 103.3, about 11 points above; consensus is not a forecast, but anyone reading it as the likely print was badly wrong (Conference Board via PR Newswire; Bloomberg, 24 Nov).
The prior brief carried a Dell EPS consensus of $6.63 (Zacks via mlq.ai). Dell reported adjusted EPS of $9.45, far above (Yahoo Finance; Benzinga, 24 Nov).

The prior brief reported Tuesday futures lower, led by the Nasdaq, and left open how much of Monday’s move would hold. The Nasdaq closed −1.48% and the S&P −0.50%; the Dow, though, rose 0.85% (Yahoo Finance; Kotak Neo, 24 Nov).

The prior brief put October PCE and the Q3 GDP second estimate on Wednesday at 8:30 ET and said markets close Thursday; confirmed by Wednesday-morning previews (Admiral Markets; Yahoo Finance, 25 Nov).
The prior brief listed the Richmond Fed manufacturing index (consensus −3); the actual reading was not confirmed in this morning’s search and is left ungraded.
